chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Muthanna al-Hannat from Zurara from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a crop that was sold while it was still grass (unripe), and later became ears of grain (ripe), he said: 'There is no harm if he says, I buy from you what emerges from this crop. So when he buys it while it is still grass, if he wishes, he can let it remain in the ground, and if he wishes, he can wait for it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a crop before it is fully ripe in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted through the reliable chain of Zurarah, clarifies the permissibility of selling crops while still in the grass stage (Bay' al-Hasha), provided the sale is specific to what emerges from the land. It highlights the buyer's autonomy to either let the crop mature naturally or harvest it early, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of avoiding excessive uncertainty (Gharar) in agricultural transactions. This ruling is foundational in Usul al-Fiqh for distinguishing between valid conditional sales and those void due to ambiguity in the subject matter.
